questions.q: Where do the August order CSV files actually live for this project?
options: s3://northfield-raw-zone/orders-raw/, one CSV file per day, flat with no date subfolders
In a Redshift table, already loaded from the on-prem SQL Server
On the Operations Manager's local laptop, not yet uploaded to AWS
s3://northfield-raw-zone/orders/dt=2026-08-01/ with full date partitioning already in place
questions.explain: The files sit flat in one prefix, orders-raw/, with no date partitioning yet — that's the deliberate, simplest starting layout for this project.

questions.q: Which columns does each order CSV file contain?
options: product_category only, with no order-level detail
order_id, order_date, product_category, product_name, quantity, unit_price, customer_region
order_id, order_date, and a pre-calculated total_revenue column
order_id, customer_name, credit_card_number, shipping_address
questions.explain: Those seven columns are exactly what's in the raw export, and they include everything the stakeholder's question needs to compute.

questions.q: Why is there no _SUCCESS marker file or automated ingestion job for this upload?
options: S3 does not support marker files of any kind
This is a one-time manual upload for an ad hoc question, not a recurring scheduled pipeline that needs to verify completeness automatically
The Operations Manager does not have permission to upload to S3
_SUCCESS markers are only used by Redshift, never by S3
questions.explain: Marker files and automated completeness checks belong to a recurring, scheduled ingestion job — this is a one-off manual upload, so a quick manual check is enough.

questions.q: What does `aws s3 ls s3://northfield-raw-zone/orders-raw/ --summarize --human-readable` help confirm?
options: The total object count and total size for the prefix, as a quick sanity check that all 31 daily files uploaded and none are suspiciously empty
The exact schema (column names and types) of each CSV file
The IAM permissions attached to the S3 bucket
Whether the Glue Crawler has already run against this prefix
questions.explain: The --summarize flag prints a total count and size, which is a fast way to check nothing is missing or zero bytes before cataloging it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson choose a flat, unpartitioned prefix instead of uploading the files already organized by date?
options: It's the honest, simplest starting state for a one-off ask, and it sets up exactly what Lesson 8 later revisits once faster or cheaper repeated access matters
Glue Crawlers cannot read partitioned S3 prefixes at all
Athena only supports querying flat, unpartitioned data
Partitioned prefixes require a paid AWS feature not available to this account
questions.explain: Starting flat matches the real scenario, and Lesson 8 deliberately comes back to this same prefix to introduce partitioning and its benefits.
